title: QR Code Generator
description: Static QR codes for a website, WhatsApp chat, Wi-Fi, contact card, email, phone or text. Saves as PNG or SVG, prints, and never expires because nothing is redirected.
longDescription: A free QR generator that treats the code as what it is: text stored in a pattern. There is no redirect service, so a printed code keeps working and nothing you type, including a Wi-Fi password, is sent to a server. Colours, a caption, size and damage tolerance are optional, with a warning when the colours risk an unreadable code.
highlights: Fully client-side: no API route, nothing is uploaded or stored
Static codes, so there is no redirect that can lapse and no subscription
Seven content types, each validated with a plain-language message (country code for WhatsApp, WPA password length for Wi-Fi)
Contrast check that warns about light-on-dark or low-contrast colours before printing
Save as PNG or SVG through the system Save dialog where the browser has one, or print

caseStudy.problem: Most free QR generators create dynamic codes that route through the vendor's short link. They look free, then stop working when a trial or subscription ends, and the person who printed a thousand flyers finds out too late.
caseStudy.approach: Generate static codes entirely in the browser. The payload for each type follows the format phones already understand: a wa.me link for WhatsApp, the WIFI: scheme for Wi-Fi, a vCard for contacts, mailto: and tel: for the rest.
decisions: Static only. A dynamic code needs a server that stores your link and keeps redirecting it; that breaks the promise that nothing leaves the browser.
Validate on the way in. WhatsApp links with a leading 0 or a missing country code fail silently, so the form says what is wrong instead of producing a dead code.
Warn about colours rather than block them. Light-on-dark codes fail on many cameras, but the person may know their scanner.
